search_log: Searched “Stephen King Never Flinch official excerpt publisher” and “Never Flinch Stephen King excerpt chapter”; found and opened the sustained Barnes & Noble exclusive excerpt and the official Simon & Schuster page.

Searched “Never Flinch Stephen King point of view third person narrator review” and exact variants using “third person” and “third-person”; found an explicit third-person-omniscient scene analysis and a reader discussion mentioning third-person narration.

Searched “Never Flinch alternating point of view Holly Gibney Trig Saraj” and “Never Flinch multiple points of view”; reviews described multiple character focalizers and story threads, but no sustained change from third-person to first- or second-person base narration.
Checked the Hachette UK Read Excerpt control, but it returned the product page rather than accessible excerpt prose.
Checked Google Books; the located edition had no preview and supplied only catalog copy.
Ran targeted searches for ambiguous Goodreads quotations; they did not yield reliable context for the isolated I-statement or “The bastards don’t get to win.”
person_note: The controlling narration is third person, shifting focal attention among Holly, Trig, Izzy, and other characters. Several Goodreads event passages independently show external third-person scene narration, while the authorized interior excerpt sustains the same form and explicitly separates Trig's first-person direct thoughts from the narrating voice. The isolated first-person quotation is therefore local speech, thought, or commentary rather than evidence of a participating narrator. Reviews report multiple viewpoints and intertwined plots, but no credible source indicates sustained first- or second-person base sections; the remaining uncertainty is limited to the local attribution of clipped quotations, not the book-level person.
